newsitem.title: USA: AMP backs '97 yr EPS of $2.11-$2.13/share.
newsitem.headline: AMP backs '97 yr EPS of $2.11-$2.13/share.

text.p: AMP Inc, the world's leading supplier of electrical connectors, is ready to complete its restructuring by the end of the third quarter and is on track to meet earnings projections for full year.
AMP today reported second quarter results that exceeded Wall Street's consensus expectations.
William Hudson, AMP chief executive and president, said, "We remain comfortable with analyst (full-year) earnings per share estimates in the range of $2.11 to $2.13."
He added, "We continue to expect virtually all restructuring actions to be taken by the end of the third quarter."
AMP rose nearly 2-1/2 at the opening Wednesday before subsiding to 48-13/16 at mid-morning, up 1-13/16. The stock is trading at record year levels.

AMP said second quarter earnings were $0.54 per share, before a $17.7 million, or $0.05 a share, legal charge, versus $0.53 per share in the year-ago second quarter. Analysts' consensus estimate for the quarter was $0.51, according to First Call.
The legal charge was taken to reflect a recent arbitration award against AMP's Connectware unit. The award is being appealed.
Second quarter operating income of $189.3 million was up 8.4 percent from a year ago, representing a second straight quarter of sequential improvement.
"Obviously, our market penetration and cost reduction programs are showing results," Hudson said.
Annualized pretax savings from restructuring are estimated to be $50 million when fully realized, AMP said in a statement.

But Hudson cautioned that as the loss of sales from restructuring begins to take its toll, the company faces challenges to continue to improve sales growth and achieve significant additional expense savings.
Still, he said, "We are confident that we have the plan and organization in place to meet these challenges."
Second-quarter sales were $1.468 billion, a 7.5 percent increase over a year earlier, the company said.
In local currency terms, revenues grew 11.8 percent, but further strengthening of the dollar cut reported revenues by $58 million from a year earlier.

Bookings for the quarter were $1.50 billion, up 4.9 percent over the first quarter. Order backlog stood at $1.04 billion at the end of the second quarter, up $33 million from the end of the first quarter.
Among its larger markets, sales gains were strongest in the computer and communications markets. Sales growth was positive across most of AMP's major market categories.
"Sales were...up across most of our products and all three of our geographies," Hudson said.
Accounting for 50 percent of the AMP total, sales in the Americas showed improvement -- up 9 percent -- with solid growth continuing in the computer markets.
U.S. sales were up 8 percent, while Canada and Mexico led the rest of the Americas with strong double-digit growth.

Despite the underlying sluggish economies, AMP European sales -- 30 percent of the worldwide total -- were up almost 11 percent in local currencies, and up about 2 percent when translated into dollars.
Germany growth was about 11 percent in local currency, buoyed by automobile exports. Northern Europe and Spain continued their pattern of strong growth, the company said.
Asia/Pacific sales -- 20 percent of AMP's worldwide total -- grew 21 percent in local currencies, 13 percent in dollars.
Japan grew almost 10 percent in local currencies, while the company posted extremely strong sales growth in Singapore, Hong Kong and Korea.
Second quarter capital spending was $109 million, flat with last year. This brings the year-to-date spending to $230 million, with full year expectations of about $550 million.
